frame: Rater frame: conservative home-layer test. If the assigned failure mode remains open, do not give 2. If evidence is a draft, optional extension, or marketing page, cap the cell at 1. Prefer the lower score when mixed.

C.promise: Signed mandates commit agents to payment intent (moral hazard/commitment).
C.evidence: Intent/Cart Mandates signed as W3C VCs; chain of evidence described.
C.failure: Revocation not propagated into settlement; signature does not guarantee faithful execution.
C.metric: No revocation latency or scope-violation metric specified.

I.promise: Bind AP2 mandates across Web2 and Web3 rails.
I.evidence: Payment-agnostic cards/stablecoins/bank; A2A x402 extension; UCP binding.
I.failure: Cross-layer binding is optional/one-sided; no auditable conformance test.

A.promise: Deliver assurance via authorization, execution, audit artifacts.
A.evidence: VC mandates and chain of evidence; no finality/pricing/compliance/recovery artifacts.

EM.promise: Operate where banking/court/ID institutions are weak.
EM.evidence: Supports stablecoins and bank transfers; no dispute forum.
EM.failure: Still needs legal/platform fallback for remedy.
EM.metric: No weak-institution deployment or artifact metric.

S.evidence: Public GitHub repo and 60+ collaborators; positioned with A2A/MCP.
S.failure: No versioned spec or named governance; repo thin.

C.failure: No atomic bind of delivery to finality.

I.failure: Facilitator trust limits full seam propagation.
I.metric: Proof verified; settlement relies on facilitator.

A.evidence: Auth via signature; audit via proof/tx; no KYC/refund.

EM.promise: Works without banks/courts/ID via crypto wallet.
EM.failure: Still needs trusted facilitator and stablecoin access.

S.evidence: Linux Foundation x402; multiple SDKs/middleware; IETF drafts.
S.failure: Core spec versioning not independently audited.

C.promise: Portable order lifecycle state across merchants
C.evidence: Order object with fulfillment events and refund adjustments in spec
C.failure: Post-purchase state remains merchant-specific; webhooks optional

I.promise: Interoperate with AP2, MCP, A2A via well-known profile
I.evidence: Capability negotiation and version dates in business profile
I.failure: No verified end-to-end propagation across all seams

A.promise: Covers auth, execution, audit, refund properties
A.evidence: OAuth identity linking; order/refund objects; AP2 mandates

EM.failure: Depends on banking/card rails; no alternative settlement

S.evidence: Versioned spec at ucp.dev/latest; co-developed by large firms
S.failure: No independent implementation count; lodging/food incomplete

C.promise: Portable identity and behavioral trust via registries.
C.evidence: EIP-8004 defines identity, reputation, validation registries.
C.failure: Cannot cryptographically guarantee capabilities; Sybil inflation.
C.metric: Reputation score via getSummary with client filter.

A.evidence: Only auditability partially addressed via on-chain feedback.

EM.promise: Works without courts/cards/banks via blockchain identity.
EM.failure: Requires blockchain access; no loss-bearer artifact yet.

C.promise: Capability discovery and tool invocation solve discovery/effort problems.
C.evidence: Versioned spec defines prompts, resources, tools; tool-call logs exist.
C.failure: Advertised capability not bound to demonstrated performance; intent fidelity unproven.
C.metric: Validation rate of discovered capabilities; none specified.

I.promise: Connects AI apps to tools across clients and servers, enabling interop.
I.evidence: Clients include Claude/ChatGPT/VS Code/Cursor; UCP treats MCP as transport.
I.failure: No propagation of trust/payment guarantees across layer seams or Web2-Web3.
I.metric: Number of interoperable client/server pairs; no cross-layer audit metric.

A.promise: Authorization and auditability are addressed; other assurance properties absent.
A.evidence: User-mediated delegated access; tool-call logs as evidence records.
A.failure: No economic finality, pricing, compliance, or recoverability artifacts.
A.metric: 2 of 7 properties partially artifacted; count in spec.

EM.promise: Works without courts, banks, cards, or formal ID for core tool use.
EM.evidence: Open internet standard; no bank/ID/court dependency in spec.
EM.failure: No loss-bearer artifact or accountability when institutional support is weak.
EM.metric: Operations usable without those institutions; no metric defined.

S.promise: Stable, versioned open standard with broad independent adoption.
S.evidence: Versioned docs 2026-07-28; listed clients Claude/ChatGPT/VS Code/Cursor.
S.failure: Named governance body not explicitly identified in reviewed packet.
S.metric: Spec version and count of independent client implementations.

C.promise: Agent Card provides machine-readable capability advertisement for discovery.
C.evidence: Live spec defines Agent Card JSON with skills, endpoint, auth requirements.
C.failure: No validation binds advertised capability to demonstrated performance; intent fidelity unproven.
C.metric: No checkable capability-performance metric; task traces only.

I.promise: Agents interoperate over HTTP with typed tasks, messages, and artifacts.
I.evidence: Spec defines JSON-RPC polling, SSE, webhooks; MCP/x402/AP2 pairings.
I.failure: Cross-seam propagation to Web3/payments is optional adapter, not native.
I.metric: No spec-level verifiable cross-layer binding; adopters cited only.

A.promise: Assurance coverage: task traces for auditability.
A.evidence: Task ID and message/artifact history allow reconstruction; no payment/consent.
A.failure: Other six properties absent; no authorization, finality, pricing, compliance, recovery.

EM.promise: Works over plain web transport without banks, courts, cards, or platform.
EM.evidence: Direct HTTP endpoints self-describe auth; no institutional dependency.
EM.failure: No settlement, escrow, or remedy artifact; loss-bearer has no recourse.
EM.metric: Institutional dependence low; no inspectable loss artifact -> score 1.

S.evidence: Linux Foundation TSC (AWS, Google, IBM, MS, Salesforce, SAP, SN); 6 SDKs.
S.failure: None named; governance and independent implementations present.
S.metric: Named governance plus multiple independent SDKs/implementations.

C.promise: Event protocol surfaces agent state and UI intents for user oversight.
C.evidence: Docs list streaming chat, thinking-step visualization, interrupts.
C.failure: T5 open: interface transparency does not close weaker seams.

I.promise: No cross-layer or Web2-Web3 binding specified.
I.evidence: Positions next to MCP/A2A; framework integrations only.
I.failure: Connectivity without propagation; no auditable binding.

A.promise: Addresses one property partially via HITL interrupts.
A.evidence: Interrupts (pause, approve, edit, retry) in docs.
A.failure: No mandate, settlement, or dispute objects.

EM.promise: No reduction of dependence on missing institutions.
EM.evidence: Docs contain no banking, ID, enforcement, stability artifacts.
EM.failure: Requires functioning platform/delivery; no loss-bearer artifact.

S.promise: Open protocol with multiple framework integrations.
S.evidence: GitHub repo, docs, SDKs for Kotlin/Go/Dart/Rust.
S.failure: No versioned spec or named governance in packet.

C.promise: Decentralized arbitration and enforceable escrow for contract disputes.
C.evidence: Live court since 2019; whitepaper, ERC-792/1497, Escrow product.
C.failure: Days-scale latency; no agent-speed enforcement standard.
C.metric: Dispute resolution latency from court logs (unpublished here).

I.promise: Arbitration/evidence interface bindable by external smart contracts.
I.evidence: ERC-792 and ERC-1497 documented on docs site.
I.failure: Optional, one-sided integration; not default for AP2/x402/UCP.
I.metric: Count of external protocols with auditable ERC-792 binding.

A.promise: Evidence and appeal mechanism provide auditability and recoverability.
A.evidence: ERC-1497 evidence records; escrow and appeals in docs.
A.failure: Authorization, pricing, and compliance not enforced by Kleros.

EM.promise: Dispute resolution without courts, banks, or formal ID.
EM.evidence: Crowdsourced jury, crypto wallets, no KYC, on-chain escrow.
EM.failure: Cross-jurisdiction recognition not automatic; needs crypto access.

S.promise: Stable public specification with governance and ERC standards.
S.failure: Limited independent implementers; corpus has only 3 OA records.
